name: Vowelconsonantsplitreversecipher

description_json.name: VowelConsonantSplitReverseCipher
description_json.idea: To maximize the model's reasoning capabilities and prevent garbled outputs, we use a highly intuitive, structured, and reversible character-level mapping. We reverse the order of vowels and consonants separately within their respective alphabets. Specifically, vowels (A, E, I, O, U) are mapped to their exact reverse (A<->U, E<->O, I<->I). Consonants are mapped to their exact reverse in the 21-consonant alphabet (B<->Z, C<->Y, D<->X, F<->W, G<->V, H<->T, J<->S, K<->R, L<->Q, M<->P, N<->N). Case is preserved. Non-alphabetic characters (spaces, punctuation, digits) remain completely unchanged.
description_json.encrypt_rules:
For each character in the text:
1. If it is a vowel, map it using the reversed vowel sequence: A <-> U, E <-> O, I <-> I, O <-> O, U <-> A (and similarly for lowercase: a <-> u, e <-> o, i <-> i, o <-> o, u <-> a).
2. If it is a consonant, map it using the reversed consonant sequence: B<->Z, C<->Y, D<->X, F<->W, G<->V, H<->T, J<->S, K<->R, L<->Q, M<->P, N<->N (and similarly for lowercase: b<->z, c<->y, d<->x, f<->w, g<->v, h<->t, j<->s, k<->r, l<->q, m<->p, n<->n).
3. If it is any other character (space, digit, punctuation), leave it unchanged.
description_json.decrypt_rules:
Since the mapping is a set of simple bijections (swaps), decryption uses the exact same rules as encryption:
1. If it is a vowel, map it using the reversed vowel sequence: U <-> A, O <-> E, I <-> I, O <-> O, A <-> U (and similarly for lowercase).
2. If it is a consonant, map it using the reversed consonant sequence: Z<->B, Y<->C, X<->D, W<->F, V<->G, T<->H, S<->J, R<->K, Q<->L, P<->M, N<->N (and similarly for lowercase).
3. If it is any other character, leave it unchanged.
